response.title: Defer a Unified Streaming Recovery Policy
response.summary: The evidence supports four distinct recovery policies: preserving server retry deadlines, continuing a stream after visible output, failing over after consecutive no-progress responses, and admitting one recognized transport code to an existing retry classifier. These policies share a broad recovery theme but do not provide a coherent set of required roles independently realized in at least two repositories.
when_to_use: Use the supported workflow-specific fragment when the observable failure signal exactly matches its preconditions: server retry advice, a retryable stream cut with tracked output state, consecutive incomplete responses with no visible answer or tool call, or a stable premature-close transport code.

Use this deferred result when considering a common recovery abstraction across repositories and the available implementations differ in semantic owner, state transition, safety boundary, or validation oracle.
Reconsider induction only after an untouched repository demonstrates the same required role contracts and ordering as one of the supported fragments.
anti_goals: Do not treat retry timing, retry eligibility, output continuation, and fallback handoff as interchangeable recovery operations.
Do not infer that all partial stream failures are safe to replay or continue.
Do not let server timing advice authorize a retry that existing eligibility or budget policy rejects.
Do not persist request-scoped continuation instructions or protocol-specific replay artifacts as canonical conversation history.
Do not broaden retry budgets, allocate repeated grace calls, or introduce unbounded recovery.
Do not promote a cross-project pattern solely because the workflows share a contract-first or classify-then-repair control-flow shape.
not_applicable_when: The failure is terminal, explicitly cancelled, or unsafe to retry because replay could duplicate external side effects.
The runtime cannot distinguish caller-visible output, internal reasoning, blank output, and structured calls.
No stable transport classification, retry-advice boundary, continuation contract, or configured fallback mechanism exists for the observed failure.
The proposed change concerns only one repository-specific representation and has no independently supported cross-repository role contract.
invariants: Retry eligibility and retry budgets remain independently authoritative; timing advice or partial progress does not expand them.
Already visible output must not be silently duplicated, discarded, or represented differently in durable history after successful recovery.
Temporary recovery metadata must remain scoped to the request or protocol that understands it.
Recovery stops when its bounded budget is exhausted or when the operation becomes unsafe.
Error and retry telemetry retain the concrete failure information required by the applicable workflow.
Distinct Action contracts remain distinct even when their workflows occupy similarly named control-flow roles.

action_template.title: Capture retry advice once
action_template.purpose: Normalize valid relative or date-based server retry advice at receipt into a monotonic deadline while distinguishing absent, invalid, expired, and explicit-zero advice.
action_template.condition: Applicable only when an unsuccessful response or streamed error supplies server retry timing.
action_template.validation: Focused clock-controlled parsing checks cover supported formats, countdown behavior, zero and expired advice, malformed values, and overflow.

action_template.title: Preserve the deadline across errors
action_template.purpose: Carry the originally captured deadline through error translation, provider rewriting, protocol boundaries, and retry exhaustion without restarting its countdown.
action_template.condition: Applicable only when the failure crosses one or more error-representation boundaries before scheduling.
action_template.validation: Mapping checks assert deadline identity, decreasing remaining time after virtual-time advances, and zero rather than absence after expiry.

action_template.title: Schedule against the preserved deadline
action_template.purpose: For an independently eligible retry within budget, wait until the preserved server deadline or use the established local backoff when no valid deadline exists.
action_template.condition: Applicable only after existing policy declares the failure retryable and confirms remaining budget.
action_template.validation: Paused-time and end-to-end checks verify original-deadline timing, local-backoff fallback, bounded request count, telemetry, and terminal behavior.

action_template.title: Fold delivered text without overlap
action_template.purpose: At each failed stream-attempt boundary, add unique visible text to the accumulated prefix and remove replayed tail overlap.
action_template.condition: Applicable when repeated stream attempts can deliver text before terminating and a continuation lifecycle tracks that text.
action_template.validation: Repeated-cut checks prove that each visible fragment appears exactly once and that the per-attempt buffer is cleared.

action_template.title: Choose replay, continuation, or stop
action_template.purpose: Select bounded replay only before nonblank visible output, bounded continuation only when visible text exists without an emitted structured call, and propagation otherwise.
action_template.condition: Applicable after a retryable stream cut has been classified and current output and structured-call state are available.
action_template.validation: Focused boundary checks cover no output, blank output, reasoning-only output, visible text, structured calls, repeated cuts, and exhausted budgets.

action_template.title: Stage continuation context for one request
action_template.purpose: Place the delivered prefix and overlap-averse resume instruction only in the next request while signaling that the consumer must retain its current output buffer.
action_template.condition: Applicable only when continuation was selected and a nonblank delivered prefix exists.
action_template.validation: Request-shape and event checks verify the temporary turns, continuation signal, ordered caller chunks, and absence of synthetic turns from durable history.

action_template.title: Reconcile output and durable history
action_template.purpose: On continuation success, merge the delivered prefix into one complete durable model response; when a fresh restart supersedes continuation, clear all staged state first.
action_template.condition: Applicable after successful continuation or whenever another recovery path replaces staged continuation.
action_template.validation: History checks cover ordinary text, leading reasoning, reasoning-only completion, deduplication, and clean restart paths.

action_template.title: Detect consecutive no-progress responses
action_template.purpose: Track a per-turn streak of incomplete responses containing neither visible answer text nor a tool call, resetting the streak whenever observable progress occurs.
action_template.condition: Applicable when incomplete responses are returned as normal protocol results rather than transport exceptions.
action_template.validation: State checks prove that only consecutive no-answer and no-tool responses increment the streak and that visible progress resets it.

action_template.title: Hand off a stalled turn with bounded grace
action_template.purpose: Activate the configured fallback chain after the stall threshold, retain the same turn, and reserve at most one extra call if the normal budget was consumed.
action_template.condition: Applicable when the no-progress threshold is reached and a configured fallback can be activated.
action_template.validation: Recovery and budget checks verify the typed fallback reason, completed answer, exact call count, counter reset, and one consumed grace flag.

action_template.title: Sanitize a cross-protocol fallback request
action_template.purpose: Project canonical history into a fallback-compatible request without source-only continuation markers or opaque reasoning replay state, while preserving valid role alternation.
action_template.condition: Applicable only when fallback activation changes to a protocol that cannot consume the source protocol's recovery artifacts.
action_template.validation: Wire-level checks verify artifact removal and role alternation while confirming canonical stored history remains unchanged.

action_template.title: Admit one recognized stream-close code
action_template.purpose: Add a stable premature-close transport code to an existing bounded network-retry classifier while preserving the concrete code in retry telemetry.
action_template.condition: Applicable only when the exact code is reproduced during stream iteration, is known to be transient, and the existing retry path safely covers the operation.
action_template.validation: A streaming regression emits partial content, throws the exact code, observes a retry event, receives complete later output, and records the exact telemetry type.

branches.condition: The response carries valid server retry timing that must survive layered propagation.
A retryable stream cut occurs after zero or more chunks may have reached the caller.
Consecutive incomplete responses contain neither visible answer text nor a tool call.
Stream iteration fails with the exact recognized premature-close transport code and an existing bounded retry path applies.

decision_points.question: After a retryable stream cut, is replay or continuation safe?

branches.condition: No nonblank caller-visible text has accumulated and replay budget remains.
Nonblank visible text has accumulated, no structured call was emitted, continuation is representable, and continuation budget remains.
A structured call was emitted, a required capability is absent, or the applicable budget is exhausted.

decision_points.question: Does fallback activation cross an incompatible protocol boundary?

branches.condition: The destination cannot consume source-only continuation markers or opaque reasoning replay state.
The destination uses the same compatible protocol and no incompatible artifacts are present.

ordering_constraints.condition: When server retry advice crosses an error-mapping boundary.
When an eligible retry is scheduled after one or more error translations.
Only when the selected mode is continuation.
When a staged continuation succeeds or is superseded by a fresh restart.
When the configured consecutive-stall threshold is reached.
When the activated fallback uses an incompatible destination protocol.

validation_ladder: Focused contract checks: test each selected Action contract at its local boundary, including exact error classification, retry-advice parsing, stall-counter reset, recovery-mode selection, overlap removal, request-scoped metadata, and protocol projection.

Integration checks: exercise the applicable recovery path across its real boundaries, including transport-to-error-to-scheduler propagation, partial-stream failure followed by a successful attempt, or same-turn fallback activation with exact budget accounting.

Regression checks: verify terminal classifications remain terminal, retry and grace budgets remain bounded, no-advice failures retain local backoff, visible output is neither duplicated nor discarded, canonical history contains no synthetic recovery artifacts, structured-call ordering remains valid, and telemetry retains the concrete failure type.
Cross-repository promotion check: require at least two repositories to independently realize every proposed required role with matching semantic owner, pre-state, post-state, and validation oracle.
Holdout check: after training support exists, validate the complete proposed policy on a separate untouched repair before candidate promotion.

known_failure_modes.failure: A relative retry delay is reconstructed after propagation and starts counting down again.
known_failure_modes.detection: Virtual-time checks show the remaining wait resetting or increasing after error translation or notification work.
known_failure_modes.mitigation: Capture one monotonic deadline at receipt, preserve its identity, and schedule from its remaining duration.

known_failure_modes.failure: A fresh replay duplicates text that was already delivered to the caller.
known_failure_modes.detection: A partial-output regression produces repeated fragments in caller output, the next request, or durable history.
known_failure_modes.mitigation: Select replay only before nonblank visible output; otherwise use bounded continuation with overlap reconciliation or propagate.

known_failure_modes.failure: Continuation inserts an invalid turn after an emitted structured call.
known_failure_modes.detection: Recovery-mode boundary checks observe a function call before the cut.
known_failure_modes.mitigation: Reject continuation for that attempt and propagate or use another independently safe recovery path.

known_failure_modes.failure: Protocol-specific recovery artifacts leak into a fallback request or canonical history.
known_failure_modes.detection: Wire or history assertions find synthetic continuation instructions, markers, or opaque reasoning replay fields.
known_failure_modes.mitigation: Keep continuation context request-scoped and sanitize only the outbound fallback projection.

known_failure_modes.failure: Recovery silently expands retry or iteration budgets.
known_failure_modes.detection: Request-count assertions exceed configured retries or more than one fallback grace call is consumed.
known_failure_modes.mitigation: Retain independent bounded budgets and permit only the explicitly supported single grace call.

known_failure_modes.failure: A broad exception class is admitted as retryable when only one stable transport code is supported.
known_failure_modes.detection: Static or classifier tests show generic exception matching or unrelated codes entering the retry path.
known_failure_modes.mitigation: Add only the exact reproduced code to the existing bounded classifier and retain it in telemetry.

exclusions: Retry exhaustion redesign, unbounded connection retry, and changes to retry-count policy.
Generic exception retryability without a stable, reproduced transient classification.
Recovery for caller cancellation, explicit aborts, policy refusals, malformed requests, or non-replayable side effects.
Provider or protocol fallback when no configured fallback mechanism exists.
Universal transcript sanitation when the destination protocol is already compatible.
Claims that the supplied Actions are substitutes for one another merely because they classify, reconcile, adapt, or repair recovery state.
response.rationale: No required role can be bound to matching Action contracts in at least two supplied repositories. The retry-deadline workflow controls timing metadata, the stream-continuation workflow controls caller-visible and durable output state, the stalled-turn workflow controls semantic fallback and protocol adaptation, and the premature-close workflow narrowly changes transport classification. The factorization audit explicitly identifies cross-repository comparisons as different owners, preconditions, postconditions, and validation oracles. Combining them would produce a category-level label rather than an evidence-grounded decision policy. Because no holdout is loaded and the training evidence supports only separate fragments, candidate_pending_holdout is not permitted.
missing_probes: A second repository independently implementing receipt-time retry-deadline capture, cross-layer preservation, and deadline-based scheduling with matching state and timing oracles.
A second repository independently implementing output-aware replay-versus-continuation selection, request-scoped continuation, overlap reconciliation, and durable-history repair.
A second repository independently implementing consecutive no-progress detection and same-turn fallback with the same bounded grace-call contract.
Evidence that a common required role sequence applies across these failure classes without merging timing, classification, continuation, and fallback Action contracts.
A separate untouched holdout repair validating any future coherent cross-repository policy.
